suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-22 adds this relationship only as a bounded post-torsion outcome proposition. The cited pediatric surgical cohort found that testicular atrophy can develop after attempted salvage for testicular torsion, with risk related to factors including symptom duration and intraoperative testicular appearance; it does not establish that every individual's atrophy was caused by torsion or exclude pre-existing, congenital, infectious, traumatic, or other causes. Require documented testicular torsion, separately documented later ipsilateral testicular atrophy or objective volume loss, and compatible chronology. Preserve delayed presentation, degree and duration of ischemia, orchiopexy or other treatment, infection, trauma, cryptorchidism, congenital hypoplasia, and contralateral or bilateral disease as competing explanations. Do not infer atrophy from a torsion history alone or from postoperative symptoms without objective examination or imaging.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of testicular torsion and later testicular atrophy
Serial testicular examination or ultrasound documenting objective ipsilateral volume loss
Operative findings, degree/duration of torsion, salvage procedure, and postoperative chronology
Assessment of congenital hypoplasia, cryptorchidism, infection, trauma, and other causes of atrophy
Resolution of publication guard: Require documented torsion, objective later ipsilateral atrophy, and compatible chronology; do not infer atrophy from torsion history alone.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited pediatric surgical cohort associates testicular torsion and attempted salvage with later ipsilateral testicular atrophy in some patients, supporting focused urologic review without establishing deterministic individual causation.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established by the current evidence; objective atrophy, chronology, operative details, and competing etiologies are required for individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Twisting of the spermatic cord can impair testicular perfusion and may leave ischemic or postoperative volume loss after detorsion and salvage, but the individual mechanism remains hypothesized until objective serial atrophy and torsion-treatment chronology are documented.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Post-torsion atrophy is a recognized possible outcome after salvage, but the cited cohort does not establish that every individual's atrophy is torsion-related and requires objective chronology and competing-cause review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent torsion and atrophy diagnoses; serial objective volume measurements; operative and ischemia-duration records; and urologic assessment of congenital, infectious, traumatic, and other alternatives.
